title: Capstone: Key-Value Database
description:
```
kv> SET user:1 Ann
OK
kv> GET user:1
Ann
kv> INCR visits
1
kv> KEYS user:*
user:1
kv> SAVE
saved 2 keys
```
hints: Split each line into words, then a `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::function<std::string(const std::vector<std::string>&)>>` from command name to handler keeps `main` short.
`KEYS user:*`: take the pattern without its `*`, and list every key that starts with it (`key.starts_with(prefix)`).
requirements: `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string>` storage in a `Database` class, separate from the command line
Commands: `SET`, `GET`, `DEL`, `EXISTS`, `INCR` (a missing key counts as 0), `KEYS` with a `*` at the end matching any rest, `SAVE`, `LOAD`
Errors (unknown command, wrong number of words, `INCR` on text that is not a number) give a message, never a crash
stretch: `EXPIRE key seconds` and `TTL key` with `<chrono>`, removing a key when it is read after it expired, and values that can be lists with `std::variant`.
